title: Reading Drill — Studying book exchanges on stations — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying book exchanges on stations — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The exchange volunteer had been asked to investigate popular shelves filling with books in poor condition in Ravensmere. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the share of books suitable for exchange, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a eight-week comparison, the team used sample checks at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because station closure times might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a clear condition notice. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
